draft.change: Add a noun entry for the gentilic אַרְוָדִי. Its form derives from the place name אַרְוָד, and its use in the clan list supports the gloss “Arvadites.”
draft.definition: A member of the people of Arvad, or the people collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:18 uses the definite singular for the Arvadites in its list of Canaanite clans.

analysis.evidence: The repeated וְאֶת places הָאַרְוָדִי alongside the Zemarites and Hamathites in Canaan’s genealogy. The closing phrase מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי identifies these groups as Canaanite clans.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular gentilic noun in the absolute state. The ending ־ִי marks affiliation with Arvad. The singular names the people collectively.
analysis.sense: The people of Arvad, counted among the Canaanite clans.

draft.change: Add the gentilic צְמָרִי with its collective use in the genealogy of Canaan.
draft.definition: A Zemarite, a member of one of the Canaanite clans.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:18 names the Zemarites among the Canaanite families and uses a singular gentilic for the group.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:18 lists הַצְּמָרִי between the Arvadite and the Hamathite, introducing each with וְאֶת. The closing phrase מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי, “the families of the Canaanite,” identifies the groups just listed.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial צ of the masculine singular absolute gentilic noun צְמָרִי. The singular designates the clan collectively.
analysis.sense: A member of the Zemarite clan, here denoting the clan as a whole.

analysis.evidence: אַחַר modifies the verb נָפֹצוּ and takes no complement. After the list of Canaanite peoples, the clause states that the Canaanite clans subsequently dispersed.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ prefixes the temporal adverb אַחַר.
